title: Readers and Aggregate are built from an Atlas
body:
`atlas::Atlas` lists data files in order with each one's record count and stamp. Two `libsail` types already read several sources as one run of records, and neither can be built from an atlas:

- `index::Readers::new(paths, format)` streams the files one after another. Its `count()` opens and scans every file to learn the per-file counts that let `advance_to` skip whole files.
- `collection::Aggregate<I>` numbers several `Indexable` collections as one range. A caller builds each part (an `IndexedFasta` from its `.saidx`, for example) and hands them over.

An atlas already holds the paths, the format and the counts, so both could be built from it without a counting pass or a per-part loop in the caller.

## Options

| option | signature | cost |
|---|---|---|
| a constructor on each type | `Readers::from_atlas(&Atlas)`, `Aggregate::from_atlas(&Atlas)` | `Aggregate` is generic over its part type, so its constructor needs the part type chosen by the caller or one impl per format |
| methods on `Atlas` | `atlas.readers()`, `atlas.indexed::<IndexedFasta>()` | `atlas` depends on `collection` and `seq` |
| `From<&Atlas>` | `Readers::from(&atlas)` | the generic `Aggregate` case has the same problem as the first option |

Both constructors refuse an atlas with stale parts and name them by position (sail-978552). A part whose `.saidx` is missing or stale is refused the same way.

Leaning: a constructor on each type. `Readers` takes the counts as given and skips `count()`'s pass. `Aggregate` gets a constructor generic over a part type that can open itself from a path and its `.saidx`.
